conviction_note: Two separate measurements. The findings sum to +2.5, driven by a likely beat of the two-analyst Q2 EPS bar of $0.63. For Q1, management used the same 'slightly lower sales, lower adjusted EPS year on year' wording, consensus sat 25% below the prior year, and the print came in flat year on year, a $0.14 beat that moved the stock +15.2%. The scaled number is p_up 58 x abs 12 = +1.92. Both point the same way. The scaled number is smaller because the reaction on this name turns on the FY27 guide: a beat with a guide cut was sold (-4.4% in Oct 2025), and the H2-weighted guide rests on 'improving market conditions' that the ABI does not show yet.
bar: Q2 FY27 adjusted EPS $0.63 on revenue ~$359.5m. MarketBeat earnings preview 2026-09-29 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-apogee-enterprises-apog-set-to-release-quarterly-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/); a search snippet gives the Zacks consensus at $0.63 too (it was $0.59 on 2026-07-07, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/options/articles/options-traders-know-something-apogee-150700500.html). Two estimates only. Company guide: FY27 adjusted EPS $2.70-3.25, sales $1.43-1.48bn including Kalwall, and Q2 sales 'slightly lower' with adjusted EPS 'lower' year on year (prior-year Q2: $358.2m, $0.98). print_vs_bar is measured on EPS, the line this name trades on.
positioning_check: Short interest 4.91% of float as of 2026-09-11 (Benzinga, search snippet); another mid-September source shows 4.16% float and a 3.42-day short ratio; the sweep row gives 4.63% and 4.48 days (stockanalysis, snippet_only). The short is not crowded. No option chain was usable (skew null), so the market makes no directional statement. The stock is -10.8% over 20 days, -27% from its 52-week high and back below the pre-Q1 level (the +15% Q1 reaction fully given back). Argus cut its target to $36 on 2026-09-02. Expectations are low.

findings.finding: The $0.63 Q2 EPS bar looks set too low. For Q1, management used the identical guidance wording ('net sales slightly lower and adjusted EPS lower year over year'). Consensus then sat at $0.41-0.43 against $0.56 a year earlier, and Q1 printed $0.57, flat. Q2 consensus now sits 36% below last year's $0.98. Starting from Q1's segment EBITDA of $32.3m ($0.57), Q2's seasonal segment margins (Q2 FY26: Metals 14.8%, Glass 16.1%, Performance Surfaces 23.2%, after cutting Glass to Q1's ~9%) plus two months of Kalwall (~$85m a year at ~15% EBITDA) give roughly $0.68-0.88.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-06-26): $0.57 vs $0.41-0.43 with the guide reaffirmed, +15.2%. Q4 FY26 (2026-04-24): beat with an FY27 guide below FY26, +7.6%. Q2 FY26 (2025-10-09): $0.98 vs $0.86 but the FY guide cut, -4.4%. So beats pay when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected Q2 near $0.80, consensus would have moved toward it after the Q1 beat. Instead the Q2 number went from $0.59 (Jul 7) to only $0.63, FY consensus is $2.81 (near the $2.70 low end of the guide), and the stock trades ~12.7x that low-end number after giving back the whole Q1 reaction. With two analysts, nobody has re-modelled the Q1-to-Q2 seasonality (Q2 has run $0.39-0.42 above Q1 in each of the last two years).
findings.independence: The April call's identical Q1 wording (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/24/apogee-apog-q4-2026-earnings-transcript/) and the Q2 FY26 segment base (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684525000154/a83025fy26q2results.htm) are separate documents. The Q1 FY27 10-Q (D&A $12.6m, interest $2.8m, 21.3m diluted shares; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000063/apog-20260530.htm) supplies the bridge. The model and the wording pattern are both company-level, but this is still an inference, not a reported number.

findings.finding: The guide is H2-weighted on 'anticipated improvement in underlying market conditions', and the AIA/Deltek ABI says that improvement has not started. The August ABI was 47.2, contracting in 46 of the last 47 months, and firms expecting Q4 2026 billings to rise fell from 31% to 25% while those expecting declines rose from 21% to 29%. That raises the risk of a guide narrowed to the low end or cut, partly offset by two acquisitions that raise the sales guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cuts were sold hard: 2026-01-07 (FY guide 6% below estimates) -13.9%; 2025-01-07 -19.0%; 2025-10-09 FY26 guide lowered despite a beat, -4.4%. Reaffirmation on 2026-06-26 was bought (+15.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: FY consensus of $2.81 already sits near the $2.70 low end, and the -27% drawdown reflects demand worry. If the market fully expected a cut, consensus would already be below $2.70. The low end is fairly safe if Q2 beats (H1 ~$1.30-1.45, with H2 guided at or above H1), so the residual risk is a midpoint cut, not a collapse.
findings.independence: AIA's own release (https://www.aia.org/resource-center/abi-august-2026-architecture-firm-billings-continue-decline) is the same series. Cutting against it: Tecnoglass on 2026-08-06 reported record multifamily/commercial revenue (+15.7%) and record backlog, and Apogee's own Services backlog was $734.5m, +7.5% year on year. This is a macro proxy that no counterparty has confirmed for Apogee.

findings.finding: Aluminum input costs kept rising through Apogee's Jun-Aug quarter. Tecnoglass cut its 2026 EBITDA guide on 2026-08-06, citing all-in US aluminum up ~77% year on year and ~$17m of Section 232 cost in one quarter. That is a lagged pass-through risk to Architectural Metals (~37% of sales).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Metals margin drove the FY26 tariff-driven guide cuts (the Oct 2025 and Jan 2026 prints, -4.4% and -13.9%). In Q1 FY27 Metals margin rose +390bps on pricing and surcharges and the stock rose 15.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: This peer data point came after Apogee last spoke (06-26). It is sized small because Apogee's own Q1 number, a primary document, shows the surcharge mechanism outrunning the same inflation. Glass, Services and Performance Surfaces (~63% of sales) are not aluminum-priced in the same way.
findings.independence: Apogee's April call cited aluminum +87% year on year and +25% since January (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/24/apogee-apog-q4-2026-earnings-transcript/), which agrees on the cost. Apogee's Q1 Metals margin (+390bps) contradicts the transmission. This is a proxy.

findings.finding: GroGlass (Latvia, anti-reflective glass coatings, ~$30m revenue at ~25% adjusted EBITDA margin, about €62.5m plus up to €10m earnout, ~9-10x EBITDA, funded from cash and the revolver) closed 2026-09-23. Management said financial details would come on this Q2 call, so the sales guide rises again (Kalwall already took it to $1.43-1.48bn), and the deal buys a margin above Apogee's own.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Kalwall announcement and Q1 together drew +15.2% on 2026-06-26, but on Kalwall's closing (07-01 to 07-02) the stock fell ~7.6% as leverage worries surfaced (~2x pro forma).
findings.why_not_priced: The deal is public, but its effect on the FY27 numbers is unquantified until the call. Revolver use was read as a leverage worry after Kalwall. On the question of what the money buys: a 25%-margin coatings business with $4m of synergies, so the financing is a small positive, not distress. Leverage stays near 2x with $419m of revolver availability (10-Q).
findings.independence: The closing 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684526000093/exhibit991-pressrelease.htm, 2026-09-23) is the same company. A Seeking Alpha piece questioning the Kalwall M&A (https://seekingalpha.com/article/4912596-apogee-enterprises-questioning-the-recent-m-and-a-move) cuts the other way.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 8-Ks since Q1 (Aug 5 and Sep 14 items 5.02, routine director changes; Sep 2 / Sep 23 GroGlass): no pre-announcement, no impairment, no officer departure in Finance
Form 4s since June: only awards, a director gift and Sept/Oct director grants, no open-market selling or buying
Cause of the July-September giveback beyond the Kalwall leverage worry, Argus target cuts and the weak ABI: nothing company-specific found
Glass segment order/lead-time data from float-glass suppliers: nothing current found

rejected_candidates.candidate: Glass president Christopher Ede 'invests $402K' in APOG stock on Jul 6/21 (Benzinga headline), read as an insider buy
rejected_candidates.detail: The insider table records it as 'Purchase (Award)' of 10,115 shares at $39.79, a new-hire grant, not an open-market purchase.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Tecnoglass record commercial backlog as a positive demand read for Apogee
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged as the counterweight into the ABI guidance finding rather than filed as a separate positive on the same demand question.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew. The positive lean runs against the -10.8% 20-day and -27%-from-high tape, but that drawdown sits on a two-analyst bar near the guide's low end, so a beat plus a held guide is not in the price. The weak-ABI guide risk is the part that agrees with the tape.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 / core 'inference smaller': the Q2 beat finding rests on a seasonality model and a wording pattern, not a reported number, so it was trimmed from +4.0 to +3.5 and print_vs_bar from +18 to +15.

Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the guide-risk finding's own text says the $2.70 low end is safe if Q2 beats, and Tecnoglass and the Services backlog cut against it, so it went from -1.5 to -1.0.

Rule 5 and Rule 9 (company number beats proxy, segment net of the rest): Apogee's own Q1 Metals margin (+390bps) contradicts the aluminum-cost transmission, and Metals is ~37% of sales, so it went from -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): GroGlass revolver funding buys a 25%-margin business, so it stays signed small positive at +0.3.

Rule 1 and Rule 8 on the scaled number: the reaction is guide-driven, so p_up went from 60 to 58. Thin coverage and a guide update carrying two acquisitions moved abs_move_pct from 11 to 12, against the historical median of 12.7.

Rule 6: the bar is sourced to two agreeing estimates ($0.63 MarketBeat and Zacks) plus the company's qualitative Q2 guide, so no cap was applied. Rule 7: short interest was checked (4-5%, not crowded).
